items.weakness: Rule-based refusals (lifecycle gate, result recording, verification) are NOT persisted in the audit trail: the DENIED audit row is written inside the same transaction that the throw then rolls back. The audit log silently omits every 'why was this refused' event the mandate requires (§5: failure path + audit record), and the API_GUIDE's 'every refusal audited' statement is false for these paths.
items.improvement: Write DENIED/FAILED audit rows through ctx.audit(null, ...) (own transaction) before throwing, or catch inside the handler, roll back, then audit. Add a helper `ctx.refuse(action, aggregate, why)` that audits out-of-band and throws.
items.rationale: ctx.audit(q, ..., 'DENIED') uses the request transaction's Queryable q, then `throw refused(why)` makes PgPool.tx issue ROLLBACK (db/pg.ts:267). Only ctx.require() denials use a separate transaction (auth/context.ts audit(null, ...)).
items.validation: tests/security: POST /v1/rooms/{room}/lifecycle {to:'ACCEPTED'} on a COMMISSIONING room with unverified tests returns 422; then SELECT count(*) FROM app.audit_event WHERE correlation_id = <x-correlation-id> AND outcome='DENIED' AND action='room.lifecycle:ACCEPTED' = 1. Same for a refused POST .../results and .../verify.
items.evidence: ctx.refuse audits out of band; tests/security/site-scope.test.mjs test 3 (DENIED row after rollback). Before: refusal rows lost on rollback. After: every rule refusal recorded.

items.weakness: A site-scoped member can act outside their sites: close any work order of the tenant (by guessing/knowing WO-nnnn codes, which are sequential) and download any evidence object of the tenant by id. Role-wide notifications and the project list also expose room codes / project names from other sites. Mandate acceptance test (13) 'technician cannot read unrelated site records … file downloads' fails by construction; website Trust page claims 'every … file read checks … the site'.
items.improvement: Make site scope a single reusable predicate: (a) join work_order→room_issue→room→building in closeWorkOrder via findRoom; (b) bind evidence to a room at upload (room_id column, FK (tenant_id, room_id)) or at first citation, and apply the room predicate on download; (c) filter notifications by site via the referenced room; (d) consider a per-request `app.site_scope` setting with RLS policies on room-bearing tables so the database enforces it too.
items.rationale: closeWorkOrder looks the work order up by code only and never calls findRoom; evidenceContent looks up app.evidence_object by id only (evidence is not linked to a room/site at all); notifications() filters by to_role/to_person; projects() lists all projects. RLS enforces tenant only; site scope is an application-layer concern applied ad hoc per handler.
items.validation: tests/security: as the South-scoped technician/svcmgr: (1) POST /v1/work-orders/{WO of a North room}/close → 404; (2) GET /v1/evidence/{id uploaded against a North room}/content → 404; (3) GET /v1/notifications contains no North room code. RLS test: with app.site_scope set to South, SELECT from app.work_order joined to North rooms returns 0 rows.

items.weakness: The RBAC matrix and OpenAPI are generated from a `authority` field that the server never enforces; the real check is a hand-written ctx.require() in each handler. Any new route, or an edited handler, can diverge from the published matrix with no test failing. The 13 hand-picked 403 cases in tests/security do not cover the route×role product (34 routes × 22 roles).
items.improvement: Split the field into machine-checkable `authority: string[]` (enforced centrally in server.ts before the handler; handlers keep finer rules) and `rules: string` (prose). Generate a matrix test from the route table × app.role: every role lacking every listed authority must get 403 (or 404 after scope) on every route; every role holding one must not get 403 from the authority check.
items.rationale: router.ts declares `authority?: string | string[] // documented here; enforced inside the handler`; http/server.ts never reads route.authority. Some values are prose ('the test’s responsible personas, or cxeng'), so the field cannot be enforced mechanically as-is.
items.validation: node tests/security/rbac-matrix.test.mjs: for each route with authority[], for each seeded role, assert (holds ? status != 403 : status == 403) with a minimal valid body; the test fails if any route has authority as prose or if openapi.json's x-authority differs from the enforced list.
items.evidence: authority keys enforced centrally before the body (http/server.ts), x-authority-enforced in OpenAPI; tests/security/authority-matrix.test.mjs: 561 role×route checks; 2 handler-rule routes listed as uncovered.

items.weakness: The 'immutable, versioned baseline' (mandate §5.13, tests 26–27; website product copy) does not exist: the accepted baseline is one JSONB column on app.room that is overwritten on each ACCEPTED transition, there is no baseline table, no version number, no path from ACCEPTED/OPERATIONAL back to recommissioning, and no drift/incident/repair link. Assurance reads `room.baseline` and reconstructs devices from a revision snapshot.
items.improvement: ADR: `app.assurance_baseline` (tenant_id, room_id, version, signed_by, signed_at, design_revision, results snapshot, sha256, supersedes, reason: ACCEPTANCE|RECOMMISSION|REPAIR_VERIFIED) append-only; room keeps `current_baseline_id`; add RECOMMISSIONING transition (ACCEPTED/OPERATIONAL → COMMISSIONING with a change order) that produces a NEW version; drift/incident events reference the baseline version.

items.feature: enterprise-web / credential exfiltration via URL parameter
items.weakness: The web app takes its API origin from the page URL (`?api=`). A phishing link `https://app.<domain>/?api=https://attacker` makes the genuine app send the user's password at sign-in and every subsequent Bearer token to the attacker's origin. The only mitigation is the CSP connect-src of the bundled static server; any other hosting (CDN, Vercel, nginx) without that header is fully exposed.
items.improvement: Remove the query-string override from production builds (allow only under `--dev`), or restrict it to an allowlist baked at build time; keep the CSP; add a build-time assertion that dist/app.js does not contain `params.get("api")`.
items.rationale: Developer convenience override shipped in the production build path.
items.validation: Browser test: open app with `?api=http://127.0.0.1:9` and sign in → no request leaves to port 9 (read_network_requests) and the app reports the configured API; grep dist/app.js for 'api' query override returns nothing.
items.evidence: ?api= honoured only in --dev builds; API origin served as meta empathia-api; scripts/verify/dist-hygiene.mjs fails the build if a production bundle contains the override.

The original 6.6 MB demonstrator is not served by apps/demo/server (dist only), so the ledger's 'original stays served until migrated' guarantee (BUILD_STATUS risk #1, parity 'REGRESSION 0') does not hold for the hosted surface: for an investor, 85 of 86 areas regressed to a card.

items.feature: lead form ↔ API contract (uncommitted P2 work in the working tree; NOT at tag p1-complete)
items.weakness: When the lead endpoint is configured, every real browser submission will be rejected with 400: the form serialises FormData, so the consent checkbox is sent as the string "on" while the API schema requires `consent: bool()` and createLead checks `consent !== true`. The integration test passes only because it posts JSON `consent: true`. Secondary: per-address burst limiting trusts a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For (trivial bypass by rotating the header; no trusted-proxy setting); the disabled-form fallback says 'Use the address on the contact page' but no address exists on /contact; migration 0009 re-introduces the settable-session-variable RLS pattern (app.lead_admin / app.public_inbound) that KV-08 removed for the worker.
items.improvement: Coerce the form payload explicitly (`consent: data.consent === 'on'`), or accept 'on'/true in the schema; add a Playwright test that submits the real form against the real API; honour X-Forwarded-For only when TRUSTED_PROXY is set and the socket peer is that proxy; give leads their own policy role (as 0008 did) or at least a SECURITY DEFINER insert function; put a real contact address on /contact or change the fallback text.
items.rationale: No browser→API contract test for the form; FormData vs JSON schema mismatch; header trust without proxy configuration; RLS gate keyed on a GUC the runtime role can set.
items.validation: Browser E2E: fill and submit /request-demo against the API with data-api set → 201 and 'Received'; SELECT count(*) FROM app.public_lead = 1. Security: two POSTs with different X-Forwarded-For from the same socket count against one bucket when TRUSTED_PROXY is unset.
items.evidence: browser form sends consent boolean; X-Forwarded-For only from TRUSTED_PROXY; tests/e2e/website-lead.e2e.mjs 6/6 (real browser → real API → admin inbox). Lead policy flag pattern: ACCEPTED for operator data (set only after ctx.require; no tenant); dedicated role deferred.

items.weakness: POST /v1/auth/token runs scryptSync (N=16384) on the event loop per attempt and is throttled only by the socket-IP bucket (600/min default, no X-Forwarded-For handling): behind one reverse proxy all users share one bucket (self-DoS), and with no per-account lockout a 600/min online guess rate per IP is available. Each attempt blocks the loop for the scrypt cost, so the sign-in route is a cheap CPU-exhaustion vector for every other request.
items.improvement: Use crypto.scrypt (async) with a bounded concurrency; add a per-email failure counter with exponential delay/lockout stored in Postgres; a stricter bucket for /v1/auth/token; TRUSTED_PROXY-aware client address.
items.rationale: Synchronous KDF; rate-limit key = socket address; no account-level counter.
items.validation: Load test: 50 concurrent wrong-password sign-ins keep p95 latency of GET /health under 100 ms; 10 failures for one email within a minute → 429/423 for that email regardless of source address.
items.evidence: services/enterprise-api/src/auth/password.ts:14 `crypto.scryptSync(...)`; http/server.ts:48 `bucketKey = `ip:${req.socket.remoteAddress}``, :63 bucket checked after auth; config.ts:56 default 600/min.

items.feature: enterprise-api / rate limiting order and memory growth
items.weakness: For authenticated routes the token is verified and the principal is resolved from the database (two queries) BEFORE the rate-limit bucket is consulted, so an unauthenticated token-spray hits the database unthrottled. The `buckets` Map (and the leads `recent` Map) are never evicted: one entry per distinct client address/person for the process lifetime (memory growth under address churn). KV-04 covers only the per-process scope.
items.improvement: Take an IP-keyed token before authentication (cheap pre-auth budget), then the person-keyed bucket after; evict idle buckets on a timer (LRU/TTL); when a shared limiter arrives (KV-04) move both there.
items.rationale: Ordering in createServer; Map without TTL.
items.validation: Unit: 1000 requests with invalid tokens from one address produce ≤ RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE resolvePrincipal calls (spy on pool.query); after 10 minutes idle, buckets.size returns to 0.
items.evidence: services/enterprise-api/src/http/server.ts:49-58 (auth + resolvePrincipal) precede :62-63 (bucket.take); :22 `const buckets = new Map<string, Bucket>()` with no eviction; domain/leads.ts:19 `const recent = new Map<string, number[]>()`.

items.weakness: Idempotency is best-effort: the handler commits its own transaction, then the key is stored in a second transaction; a crash or lost connection between the two re-executes the request on retry (duplicate room/device/project/work order). Concurrent first uses are not serialised (documented), keys never expire (table growth), and the replayed response is stored whole (evidence ids etc.) with no size bound. Mandate test (32) 'retries don't duplicate funding or evidence' cannot be met by this design.
items.improvement: Reserve the key first (INSERT … status IN_PROGRESS, unique violation → 409/replay-wait), pass the reservation into the handler's transaction so the response row is finalised in the same COMMIT as the write (RequestContext carries an optional `idempotency` that tx() updates before COMMIT); expire keys after 72 h via a worker job.
items.rationale: Key reservation is outside the handler's transaction; no IN_PROGRESS state.
items.validation: Integration: two concurrent POST /v1/rooms with the same Idempotency-Key create exactly one room (count in app.room) and both responses are equal; killing the API process after the handler COMMIT but before key storage (fault injection hook) followed by a retry does not create a second room.
items.evidence: services/enterprise-api/src/http/server.ts:81-85: `const out = await route.handler(...)` then `await ctx.tx(... INSERT INTO app.idempotency_key ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING)`; docs/api/API_GUIDE.md:80-81 acknowledges concurrency and expiry gaps.

items.feature: outbox worker / batch transaction and tenant context
items.weakness: The worker processes a whole batch (50 events) inside ONE database transaction with savepoints per event: a slow or hanging handler blocks delivery of every other event in the batch and holds row locks; a crash loses the batch's progress; the documented 'in order of occurrence' is not preserved once an event is retried (later events proceed first). readModelHandler sets app.tenant_id with set_config(…, true) which persists for the rest of the batch transaction across events of other tenants — harmless today because the worker role's policies admit everything, but a latent cross-tenant footgun for any future handler that relies on tenant policies.
items.improvement: Claim with a short transaction (mark CLAIMED with a lease), process each event in its own transaction with a per-handler statement timeout, release/extend the lease; order per aggregate (serialise by aggregate_id, not globally); reset or scope the tenant GUC per event (set_config at event start and clear at end, or a SET LOCAL inside a per-event transaction).
items.rationale: tick() wraps the batch in pool.tx; savepoints instead of per-event transactions; transaction-local GUC in a multi-event transaction.
items.validation: Worker test: a handler that sleeps 5 s on event #1 does not delay delivery of event #2 beyond 1 s; a handler that throws on tenant A's event does not leave app.tenant_id set when tenant B's event is handled (assert current_setting('app.tenant_id') equals B inside the handler); kill -9 mid-batch leaves no event in a non-PENDING/DELIVERED state after the lease expires.
items.evidence: services/enterprise-api/src/worker/outbox.ts:50-70 `return await this.pool.tx({}, async (q) => { … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED … for (const e of evs) { SAVEPOINT ev …`; :17 `set_config('app.tenant_id', $1, true)`; docs/architecture/SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md:88-90 ordering claim.

items.weakness: An evidence object is not bound to a room, test, site or purpose: any evidence id in the tenant can be cited for any test, the same object can back dozens of PASS results, and a FAIL photo can be re-cited as a PASS. The media type is whatever the client declared (no magic-byte check), file names are sanitised but the content is not inspected (KV-07 scanning OPEN). Provenance-rich evidence (mandate §5.11) is therefore a hash + a claimed type.
items.improvement: Add purpose binding at upload (room_id, intended test_id or 'unbound', captured_by, captured_at, device/instrument metadata), refuse citing evidence uploaded for another room, warn/refuse reuse of one object across tests unless the test allows shared evidence; sniff magic bytes against the declared type; keep KV-07's quarantine→scan→release.
items.rationale: evidence_object has no room/test columns; recordBlockers only checks that a ref exists; uploadEvidence trusts content-type.
items.validation: Integration: evidence uploaded with room R1 cited for a test on R2 → 422; the same evidence id cited for a second test on R1 → 422 (or audited warning when allowed by the test definition); a PNG body uploaded as application/pdf → 415.
items.evidence: database/migrations/0003_commissioning_evidence.sql:63-78 (no room_id/test_id on evidence_object; FK from test_result only); services/enterprise-api/src/domain/commissioning.ts:30-36 (`mt = mediaType.split(';')[0]` from header); packages/commissioning-engine/src/recording.ts:24 only requires `ev.ref` length ≥ 4.

items.weakness: There is no measurement in the data model: test_result stores state, evidence id/kind and a free-text `instrument`. The mandate's rules 'never equate design-specified SPL with measured SPL', 'external WAV never automatically becomes calibrated dB SPL', provenance tags (SOURCE_EXTRACTED/INFERRED/SIMULATED/FIELD_MEASURED/ENGINEER_APPROVED) on measurement fields, calibration records and units are unenforceable because the values are never captured. The legacy design ontology lists 43 measurement fields (inventory __design.measurementFields) that have no home.
items.improvement: ADR + migration: app.measurement (tenant_id, room_id, test_result_id, quantity, value numeric, unit, method, instrument_id, calibration_ref, provenance enum, captured_at, captured_by, uncertainty) append-only; design targets stored separately as `design_target` with provenance MODELED/DESIGN; a CHECK/trigger that a FIELD_MEASURED row requires instrument+calibration; result labels derived from comparison rules in the engine.
items.rationale: Vertical slice ported the pass/fail workflow, not the MeasurementEvidence/FISession record types.
items.validation: Integration: recording an instrument-measured test without a measurement row with provenance FIELD_MEASURED and a calibration reference → 422; a measurement with provenance SIMULATED can never produce PASS_VERIFIED (lifecycleBlockers refuses ACCEPTED while any applicable test's current result rests on SIMULATED/INFERRED evidence).
items.evidence: database/migrations/0003_commissioning_evidence.sql:81-96 test_result columns; packages/commissioning-engine/src/recording.ts:25 `row.instrument && !ev.instrument` (string presence only); legacy/inventory/v253-inventory.json stateMachines.__design.measurementFields = 43, v25Types includes 'MeasurementEvidence', 'FISession'.

items.weakness: The Search Party graph joins by code strings, not keys: app.relationship.from_id/to_id are text codes ('R-PLN-0001', 'PA-0001', building code) with no foreign keys; removal is by code (removeDevice updates relationships by assetCode; unrelate by codes); edges can dangle or point at a renamed/recreated entity. The mandate requires 'globally unique stable IDs and explicit relationship tables; no name-based joins' and the website claims it. Each graph request also loads every live edge of the tenant into memory (documented O(edges)).
items.improvement: ADR: entity registry table (tenant_id, entity_type, entity_id uuid, code) with a unique (tenant_id, type, code); relationships reference entity uuids with FKs and ON DELETE restrictions; codes become display attributes; traversal via recursive CTE bounded by depth and scope; keep the in-memory engine for small tenants behind a size threshold.
items.rationale: Graph modelled as a free (type,id-string) edge store ported from the browser demonstrator.
items.validation: Migration test: no row in app.relationship references a (type, id) absent from the registry; deleting/removing a device leaves zero live edges referencing it; GET /v1/graph on a 50k-edge synthetic tenant completes < 500 ms without loading all edges (query plan check).
items.evidence: database/migrations/0002_core.sql:158-169 (`from_id text`, `to_id text`, no FK); services/enterprise-api/src/domain/rooms.ts:144-150 relate/unrelate by code, :275 `UPDATE app.relationship … from_id = $1` with assetCode; domain/read.ts:68 loads all edges.

items.feature: governance / separation of duties and delegation
items.weakness: A single syseng holds both room.design and room.design.approve / room.classify.approve: the person who created the design, overrode its classification and generated the drawings can approve all of them (author ≠ approver is enforced only for result verification). There is no delegation record with expiry at all (mandate §4 'delegation, approver directory and history'; acceptance test 14 'expired delegation cannot approve'). KV-11 (approving a stale revision) compounds this.
items.improvement: Add actor rules in lifecycleBlockers/approve*: approver ≠ author of the revision/drawing/classification being approved (audit-visible override only with reason by a second engineer); introduce app.delegation (grantor, grantee, authority, scope, valid_from, valid_until, revoked_at) resolved in resolvePrincipal and tested for expiry.

items.validation: Integration: the syseng who saved revision N cannot move the room to DESIGN_APPROVED (422 with reason 'author cannot approve'); a second syseng can; a delegation with valid_until in the past does not grant project.decide (403).

items.feature: legacy migration / conflicting vocabularies in the V2.5.3 inventory
items.weakness: The original carries two overlapping authorization models and two overlapping lifecycle models, and the migration has so far adopted one of each without resolving the other: (1) 14 UI roles (AZ_KEYS: visitor, employee, exec, service, svcmgr, syseng, designer, installer, cxeng, ipm, bpm, ops, steward, architect) gate the 86 areas' visibility, while 22 personas carry authorities and map to a UI role via `base`; the API seeded the 22 personas as app.role, so area/home visibility for finance, qa_reviewer, secadmin, vendor, sitechamp, facilities, dsp/video/control_eng has no definition, and visitor/employee/ops have no role. (2) The 7-state V1 room lifecycle (PLANNED…OPERATIONAL, ported) coexists with the V2.5 design_and_commissioning machine (12 states: ENGINEERING_REVIEW…FIELD_AUTHORIZED…DOCUMENTS_APPROVED…HANDED_OFF, BASELINED) and project_governance (11 states incl. HELD/REJECTED/FUNDED/SUSPENDED); the V2.5 service machine (10 states) vs work_order (2) and room_issue (2); the V2.5 document machine (10 states) has no table; V2.5 Deficiency/Incident and V1 issue are collapsed into room_issue; V2.5 Baseline vs room.baseline. (3) 86 areas plus #/suite/* aliases give several addresses per concept. Until these are resolved, every P5/P6 module will invent a third vocabulary.
items.improvement: ADR-0003 'Canonical vocabulary': one role catalogue (22 personas + public/visitor context) with an authority→area entitlement matrix generated from it (replacing areas[].roles); one ownership map of state machines: room record lifecycle (physical), project governance (commercial), delivery (V2.5 12-state) as the orchestrating machine that references the other two, service and document machines as their own tables; a record-type crosswalk (V1 entity → V2.5 type → table) committed to docs/database and used by the parity ledger; canonical route per area with aliases redirecting.
items.rationale: The demonstrator accreted V1.x, V1.4 and V2.5 layers without removing earlier ones; the inventory records them side by side.
items.validation: Script test: every area in v253-inventory.json has an entitlement row for every one of the 22 roles (ALLOW/DENY) and every legacy UI role maps to exactly one API role or the public context; every V2.5 state machine state maps to exactly one column/state of one table in docs/database/ENTITY_DICTIONARY.md; the parity ledger has no row whose 'Backed by' names an undefined table.
items.evidence: legacy/inventory/v253-inventory.json: uiRoles (14) vs personas (22, each with `base`); areas[].roles use the 14; stateMachines.project_governance / design_and_commissioning / service / document / scouter_profile vs database/migrations/0002_core.sql:88 room.lifecycle CHECK (7 states); v25Types (32) vs 32 tables of the starter; apps/demo/src/registry.ts SUB and suite aliases; apps/demo/src/App.tsx PERSPECTIVES lists the 14 UI roles while the API uses 22.

items.feature: integrations / connector status, resilience and worker identity
items.weakness: Connector status is honest (MOCK/CONTRACT_ONLY/NOT_CONFIGURED/VERIFIED, no verified adapter) but uses a vocabulary different from the mandate's and the website's (SIMULATED/PROPOSED/CONFIGURED/HEALTHY/STALE/FAILED/READ_ONLY/ACTIVE_CAPABLE); STALE exists only as an event. Health DOWN vs DEGRADED is decided by a regex on the error message; adapter error text is stored and returned verbatim (a real adapter's error could carry URLs/credentials); there is no circuit breaker (retry + rate limit only); a sync runs inside the HTTP request (blocking) when triggered via POST; the integration worker is single-tenant, impersonates the seeded human secadmin (KV-13, audit rows attributed to a person), and has no lock against two workers syncing the same tenant.
items.improvement: Map/rename to the mandate vocabulary in one place (contract enum + DB CHECK + UI status table) and derive STALE from last_success_at vs interval on read; typed AdapterError codes drive health, free text is redacted before storage; add a circuit breaker with half-open probes in withRetry's caller; run syncs only in the worker (POST enqueues an outbox job); a non-human service principal (app.person kind=SERVICE) per tenant with adapter.allowlist only; advisory lock per (tenant, key).

items.feature: private boundary for the hosted form (ADR-0001 §3)
items.weakness: What Founder Studio actually is (from source): a React hub over (a) the 8.37 MB Founder Edition demonstrator in an iframe, driven through its own persona control and read through window.__V25__; (b) 36 films resolved by a file index to the founder's machine (and absolute workspace paths under /home/claude); (c) engineering docs, selected SOURCE FILES with full contents, diagrams, release/freeze records and IP-vault records — all compiled INTO studio.js (2.2 MB) plus a 3.5 MB source map; (d) per-founder state in localStorage (theme, scenario progress, notes, last visited) and demonstrator snapshots (raw localStorage blobs) persisted to .local/snapshots by a tiny JSON API. The only access control is a per-launch key cookie on 127.0.0.1. Hosting this as-is would put INTERNAL_ONLY/RESTRICTED_IP material in a downloadable bundle behind one cookie, contrary to ADR-0001 §3 (explicit audited API operations, private storage, founder role). Also: the studio launcher and the investor demo server share default port 4310, and the API's default CORS allowlist admits that origin — the founder origin and the investor origin are indistinguishable by default.
items.improvement: Hosted-form data model (founder schema, RLS to role founder, private bucket): founder.film (key, title, series, sha256, bytes, rights_status, object_key), founder.document (id, title, group, classification, sha256, object_key), founder.source_record (path, sha256, object_key, why), founder.vault_record, founder.diagram, founder.release_check, founder.snapshot (name, data jsonb, created_by), founder.note (destination, text), founder.scenario_progress, founder.setting; serve docs/source/vault through audited GET endpoints (founder role) instead of bundling; the Founder Edition HTML and films from the private bucket via signed short-lived URLs; keep the local launcher as a separate build target that embeds data; distinct default ports/origins per application (demo 4400, studio 4310) and CORS lists per deployable; add the cross-application negative test (customer/investor token cannot read founder.*).
items.rationale: Offline-first local launcher design; generated JSON imported into the bundle 'so the studio also works when opened from disk'.
items.validation: Build assertion: the hosted studio bundle contains none of the strings from source.json/docs.json/vault.json (hash check); security test: GET /v1/founder/vault with an enterprise-tenant token → 404/403 and an audit row; with a founder token → 200 and an audit row; RLS test: empathia_app with tenant set cannot SELECT founder.*; port/origin test: `node scripts/dev.mjs` starts demo and studio on different origins and the API CORS list contains only the app origins.
items.evidence: founder schema/role/policy flag and boundary tests (tests/security/founder-boundary.test.mjs 6/6); hosted decisions workflow (tests/e2e/founder-decisions.e2e.mjs 9/9). Open: private film/doc storage behind signed URLs, bundle no longer embedding documents, separate default port.

items.feature: build / source maps and bundle composition
items.weakness: All four builds emit source maps with sourcesContent next to the bundle and the static servers serve .map files: deploying dist/ publishes the original TypeScript of the enterprise app, the demo and the Founder Studio (the latter 3.5 MB including embedded docs/sources). The mandate: 'Source minification is not IP protection… no confidential code… exposed in public bundles'. Also no route-level code splitting (single 255 KB app.js / 211 KB demo.js), and the demo bundle embeds the parity ledger.
items.improvement: `sourcemap: 'external'` written outside dist (or `linked` with maps uploaded only to the error tracker); refuse to serve *.map in production servers; add a manifest check that dist contains no .map; split routes with dynamic import when the app grows past the budget.
items.rationale: esbuild `sourcemap: true` in production builds; servers map '.map' to application/json.
items.validation: scripts/build.mjs: fails if any file under apps/*/dist matches *.map; browser test: GET /app.js.map → 404 from every serve.mjs.
items.evidence: sourcemap external → .local/sourcemaps; servers refuse .map; dist-hygiene check in scripts/build.mjs.

items.weakness: Future work is expensive because: there is no CI configuration in the repository at all (no .github/, no pipeline file) although P1 claims typecheck/lint/test/build gates; the PostgreSQL wire-protocol client (283 lines incl. SCRAM/TLS) and the JSON-schema validator are hand-written and vendored, so every security fix in `pg`/ajv must be re-derived; the API container receives the schema-owner credentials (DATABASE_URL) although the API only needs the runtime role; no statement_timeout (KV-09); no migration-down or data-migration strategy; docs (BUILD_STATUS 'P2 NOT_STARTED', '8 migrations') already drift from the working tree (0009 + leads code present).
items.improvement: Commit a CI workflow that runs scripts/build.mjs + test suites against a service Postgres and fails on NOT_RUN for critical suites; plan the `pg`/ajv swap as the first connected-environment task (DEPENDENCY_SWAPS.md already lists them); run migrations as a separate job with the owner role, API gets only APP/WORKER URLs; set statement_timeout/idle_in_transaction_session_timeout per role in migrations; add a docs drift check (migration count, route count) to the build.
items.rationale: Offline build environment; documentation written per phase without a drift check.
items.validation: A pull request that breaks tests/security is blocked by CI; `docker compose config` shows no DATABASE_URL on the api service; `SHOW statement_timeout` as empathia_app ≠ 0; scripts/build.mjs fails when docs/api/ENDPOINTS.md route count ≠ route table count or BUILD_STATUS migration count ≠ files.
items.evidence: `ls -a` shows no CI directory; services/enterprise-api/src/db/pg.ts header 'Why vendored'; http/schema.ts (73 lines, custom validator); docker-compose.yml:28 passes DATABASE_URL to the api service, main.ts never uses cfg.ownerDatabaseUrl; database/schema/schema.sql:7-9 timeouts 0; docs/BUILD_STATUS.md:14 vs database/migrations/0009_public_leads.sql.

items.weakness: There is no administrative API: no invite/create person, no membership grant/revoke, no site-scope change, no disable person (only a column grant), no tenant/site/building creation, no feature flags, entitlements, retention or delegation. Everything is seed-only (owner role). The admin UI is read-only lists. Consequently 'role switching cannot grant privileges' and 'disabled person stops at once' are tested only via the seed/superuser path, and no customer onboarding is possible without database access.
items.improvement: P4/P6 scope: audited endpoints for invitations (token, expiry), membership grant/revoke with site scope, person disable, site/building CRUD, delegation (RT-16), feature flags and entitlements tables; secadmin-only; every call writes audit and an outbox event; invitations and revocations covered by negative tests.
items.rationale: Scope: administration (D) deferred; the mandate forbids hidden UI-only admin actions, so none were built.
items.validation: Integration: secadmin invites a person with role service and site S → the person signs in, sees only S; secadmin revokes → next request 401; a designer calling the same endpoints → 403 and audited.
items.evidence: services/enterprise-api/src/modules/routes.ts (no POST/PATCH on people, memberships, sites, tenants); database/migrations/0004_platform.sql:141-143 REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE ON app.tenant, app.person FROM empathia_app; apps/enterprise-web/src/pages/Admin.tsx People() read-only.

items.weakness: app.room.rev is described as the optimistic-concurrency version but no endpoint accepts an expected revision (If-Match / `rev` in the body): two designers editing one room serialise on FOR UPDATE and silently overwrite each other's intent (last writer wins; the design re-analysis hides it). The mandate asks for optimistic concurrency.
items.improvement: Accept `If-Match: <rev>` (or body.expectedRev) on mutating room routes; refuse with 412/409 when room.rev differs; the web client sends the rev it rendered.
items.rationale: Pessimistic row lock only; API contract has no precondition.
items.validation: Integration: GET room (rev 3); PATCH with If-Match: 2 → 412 and no change; with If-Match: 3 → 200 and rev 4.
items.evidence: database/migrations/0002_core.sql:93 `rev integer … -- optimistic-concurrency version of the record`; services/enterprise-api/src/domain/rooms.ts:154 bump() increments without comparison; routes.ts PATCH /v1/rooms/:room body has no rev field.

items.weakness: Frontend state is modest (hash routes, one cache) but the cache never evicts or revalidates (stale lists after another user's change until a mutation in this tab), useQuery's fetching effect has no dependency array (runs every render, guarded only by cache state), the sign-in page hard-codes tenant 'empathia-demo' so multi-organisation selection (mandate identity requirement) is impossible in the UI, and the role picker/password UI is dev-only with no OIDC path yet (documented). Notifications link to API paths (/v1/issues/…) rather than app routes, so the Inbox links are dead for users.
items.improvement: Add staleTime/refetch-on-focus to the cache (or swap for TanStack Query when registry access exists); tenant/role selection step after sign-in driven by /v1/auth/token's 409 list; notification links as app routes (#/rooms/{code}/commissioning) generated from a single link map shared by API and web.
items.rationale: Minimal offline stand-in for React Query; dev sign-in only.
items.validation: E2E: a room changed by user B appears updated for user A within 30 s without a page reload; a person with two memberships can choose the tenant in the UI; every Inbox link resolves to a rendered page (no 'unknown route').
items.evidence: apps/enterprise-web/src/api.ts:40-49 useQuery (no TTL, effect without deps); src/pages/SignIn.tsx:21 `tenant: 'empathia-demo'`; services/enterprise-api/src/worker/outbox.ts:40 link `/v1/issues/${…}`; src/pages/Inbox.tsx.
